evidence.s1: Part-two table reports drawn bodies behind text at light 0.66–0.95 / dark 0.13–0.37, all outside the 0.39–0.49 dead band across all 8 phases and both schemes, with source/declared/drawn kept as three separate columns.
evidence.s2: One window (label) at rest in every phase capture (e.g. phase-1-light.png) plus two ornaments; no tile field.
evidence.s3: Window shorter span ~400–470 CSS px in phase captures; record's family section gives thickness 8 across the window and both ornaments.
evidence.s4: The painting fills the right ~2/3 of every phase capture, with a painted strip visible below and between the two ornaments (phase-1-light.png).
evidence.s5: Record: 'Regular variant only; no clear, no dimming layer' — every capture shows the same frosted card, no clear-glass surface anywhere.
evidence.s6: No clear glass is used anywhere on the page (record: regular variant only), so the clear-glass-over-media constraint is not engaged by this page.
evidence.s7: Record: 'tint: none' — no control in any phase capture, either scheme, carries a coloured background.
evidence.s8: Record's mechanical-ban subset: no backdrop-filter/box-shadow/border/background authored on a host; the card and ornaments read as the runtime's own glass in every capture.
evidence.s9: Record: window fixed radius 32, ornaments capsules (r26/r22), data fill and whole-work frame concentric (32−14=18, 32−28=4) — no ad hoc radius is named.
evidence.s10: Data fill, room rows and thumbnail frames are all derived from the window's r32 anchor (32−14=18, 18−12=6 per record), visible as consistently nested corners in scroller-1-bottom-light.png.
evidence.s11: The rooms and guide ornaments' inner buttons are 44-tall capsules inside 52-tall capsules (record), shown as pill-shaped prev/next and transport controls in every phase capture.
evidence.s12: Rooms (prev/index/next) and guide (transport) are two separate glass groups, together no wider than the window (record) — 2 groups, under the 3-group cap.
evidence.s13: The rooms ornament's single capsule (bottom-left, e.g. phase-3-light.png) holds the prev/next chevron icon buttons together with the '4/8' text button that opens the Rooms view (record) — an icon button and a text button share one glass background.
evidence.s14: Record's mechanical-ban subset: hosts carry no list/row/table role and no host-level styling beyond position/box/font; the glass sits on the section/nav host, not on its children.
evidence.s15: Window-to-ornament and ornament-to-ornament gaps are runtime-derived (64 px / 24 px, record) specifically to keep the three surfaces reading as separate materials, visible as the painted strip between card and pills in every phase capture.
evidence.s16: Record: 'a child scroller scrolls with scroll edges at its inner top and bottom only where content passes under them'; scroller-1-middle-light.png and scroller-1-bottom-light.png show the essay scrolling under the still card while the nav pills stay fixed.
evidence.s17: Every phase's environment is a full painting with visible structure (ice crowds, storm clouds, brushwork) behind the glass; even the softest phases (fog, thunder, phase-8-light.png) keep visible gradient/structure.
evidence.s18: Record's CONTRAST.md summary: 0 of thousands of rendered-line/mark readings (3,756+1,332+216+1,916+812+861) fall under their 4.5:1/3:1 floor, both schemes, all 8 phases.
evidence.s19: unread: Reduce Transparency (shot-reduced.png) and Reduce Motion (fix-wave section) are both tested and recorded, but Increase Contrast is never named, captured or tested anywhere in the exhibition record.
evidence.s20: Mechanical-ban subset: no background/border/scrim on any host; the environment wash that grades contrast is painted into the canvas itself (the s1 environment-grading mechanism, named as such in part one), not a scrim added beneath a regular glass host, and no clear/modal surface exists to license one.
evidence.s21: Record: 'nothing morphs and nothing materialises after mount... the runtime's press is the only glass motion' — no cross-faded glass, no menus/sheets to test emergence, and press uses the runtime's default glow/flex.
evidence.s22: Record: 'tint: none'; all labels, kickers and icons use grayscale ink tokens in every phase capture, while the paintings alone carry saturated colour.
evidence.s23: Ink tokens are fixed light/dark greys per scheme rather than colour-matched to any painting; no capture shows a label blending into the content behind it (e.g. Wind's green field, phase-6-light.png keeps dark-grey text distinct).
evidence.s24: Record: 'every readable line now takes the primary token' at medium-to-bold weight, worst line gated (CONTRAST.md); tertiary is used only on rules/ring track and quaternary is never named.
evidence.s25: The data section's darker inset fill separates it from the card (record, 32−14=18 radius) while the current room's row takes a lifted 12% white fill (record) — dark fill for separation, light fill for the selected state, no nested glass hosts.
evidence.s26: Rooms and guide are their own overlay-plane groups attached below the window, together no wider than it, held out by the runtime-derived 64 px gap (record) rather than overlapping its edge.
evidence.s27: The whole-work thumbnail sits in an opaque frame at the window's derived radius 4 (record: 32−28=4), visible in every phase capture (e.g. phase-2-light.png).
evidence.s28: No accent colour exists on the page (tint: none); the one emphasis device, the current room's lifted white fill, covers the entire row rather than a thin mark or lightweight type.
evidence.s29: Record: 'tint: none... any control colour would compete with a Caillebotte grey or a Van Gogh blue' — identity is carried entirely by the eight paintings, not by a brand-coloured window.
evidence.s30: Record: cssBody read 'two-layer' at DPR1 and 'collapsed' at DPR2, both inspected (css-fv.png shows the two-layer light form); shot-forced.png shows Canvas panels with surviving marks (borders, outline, ring); the fidelity section states the window's span 'is beyond the bed's largest scene... extrapolated, not calibration,' and no clear/dimming layer exists to flag as uncalibrated.
